findings.title: Retry increments can be lost when cron runs overlap
findings.body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded before scheduling. If two cron executions process the same reminder concurrently, they can both read the same count and write the same next value, so two failed scheduling attempts may count as only one. The `retryCount > 1` cleanup then does not enforce the intended two-failure limit. Use an atomic database increment, and guard updates against reminders that have already been scheduled.
